Let me view one reference per candidate class.
The Alternaria reference shows a dark canker at the soil line. The test image lesion appears higher on the stem. Let me check Bacterial Canker.
The Bacterial Canker reference shows internal discoloration. Let me check Phytophthora Blight and Gray Mold stems.
The Phytophthora reference shows complete stem collapse. For my 4th reference, I'll check Alternaria stem canker more closely.

The 4th reference was a microscope view of spores - not useful for visual comparison.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Stem laid on newspaper, dark brown-to-nearly-black irregular canker at a node, shriveled dead leaves at that point, rest of stem appears green. No white mycelium.
- **Alternaria ref (Bugwood_4)**: Dark brown-black canker at stem base, very similar dark coloring and irregular shape.
- **Bacterial Canker ref**: Showed internal cross-section with vascular browning - different presentation.
- **Phytophthora Blight ref**: Shows complete stem collapse/girdling - more severe than test image.

**Ruling out:**
- Gray_Mold, Sclerotinia, Southern_Blight, Rhizopus: no white mycelium or sclerotia
- Phytophthora_Blight: no complete stem collapse
- Bacterial_Wilt/Southern_Bacterial_Wilt: no ooze/bacterial streaming visible

**Best match**: The dark brown-to-black irregular canker on the stem with associated leaf death closely matches Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers. The description "large, irregularly shaped, dark-brown to almost black cankers" fits the test image well.
